body.name: \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\)
body.construction:
Fix a deterministic query
\(z_0=(z_{01}^{\top},\ldots,z_{0S}^{\top})^{\top}\in([0,1]^d)^S\), and let
\[
 \mathcal O=\sigma\!\left((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},
 (B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i},(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N}\right)
\]
be the common observable sigma-field.  A member of
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is a labelled parameter point
\[
 \xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma),
 \qquad \mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_S),
 \qquad m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S),
\]
where \(\mathbb K_\xi\) is a probability law for the complete causal-data
array at the fixed query, its observable restriction is a law on
\(\mathcal O\),
\[
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}],
 \qquad
 \Sigma=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb K_\xi}(Z_j),
\]
and the following pointwise conditions hold.  First, for every \(s,i\),
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0,
 \qquad
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\ \text{almost surely},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
\(|Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|\le B\) almost surely,
\(m_s\in\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\), and every \(X_{st}\) is observed
exactly.  Second, for every \(s,t\), \(X_{st}\) has a Lebesgue density
\(f_{st\mid z_0}\) satisfying
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every }x\in[0,1]^d,
\]
and, for every \(s\), the sequence \((X_{st})_{t=1}^{T}\) has beta-mixing
coefficients
\(\beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\) for all \(k\ge1\).  Third, with
\(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\), unit histories are conditionally
independent across \((s,i)\) given \(\mathcal X\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]=m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]=\mu_s.
\]
Fourth, the donors are independent and identically distributed, are
independent of the entire joint panel
\(((X_{st})_{s,t},(Q_{sti})_{s,t,i},(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}})_{s,i})\), and
satisfy
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd},
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.
\]
The statistical experiment reveals only \(\mathcal O\).  Every estimator
and random interval appearing in a minimax or honesty assertion is a single
\(\mathcal O\)-measurable decision rule fixed before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\)
are selected; it may not access the potential outcomes or the nuisance
labels \((\mu,m,\Sigma)\).  This is a class of fixed-query labelled kernels,
not a choice of a regular conditional version at a query-null value.
